Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

**About Blue Origin** 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

 

As a Sr. Director for Manufacturing at Blue Origin’s manufacturing, production, and launch facilities, this role will have a direct impact on the success of Blue’s mission.

We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required.

 

**About This Opportunity** 
Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking an experienced Sr. Director with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of our rocket production program. This role will span the following functional areas:

Manufacturing and Integration
 
Provides senior leadership across production operations including structural fabrication, thermal protection systems, systems integration, testing, and final assembly for Blue Origin’s booster manufacturing. Responsible for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle. This role will also provide leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.

**Key Responsibilities:** 
Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:
 

* Lead and develop teams of Managers, Senior Managers, and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

 
**Minimum Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments

 

**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, the Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma; Black Belt certification preferred
* Experience transitioning manufacturing capabilities from development and prototyping into full-rate production
* Knowledge of fabrication processes including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and non-destructive testing
* Experience with facility activation, new production line startup, or multi-site manufacturing operations
* Proficiency with MRP/ERP, PLM, and Manufacturing Execution Systems

 

Base Pay Range for:

WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

**About Blue Origin** 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

 

As a Sr. Director for Manufacturing at Blue Origin’s manufacturing, production, and launch facilities, this role will have a direct impact on the success of Blue’s mission.

We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required.

 

**About This Opportunity** 
Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking an experienced Sr. Director with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of our rocket production program. This role will span the following functional areas:

Manufacturing and Integration
 
Provides senior leadership across production operations including structural fabrication, thermal protection systems, systems integration, testing, and final assembly for Blue Origin’s booster manufacturing. Responsible for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle. This role will also provide leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.

**Key Responsibilities:** 
Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:
 

* Lead and develop teams of Managers, Senior Managers, and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

 
**Minimum Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments

 

**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, the Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma; Black Belt certification preferred
* Experience transitioning manufacturing capabilities from development and prototyping into full-rate production
* Knowledge of fabrication processes including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and non-destructive testing
* Experience with facility activation, new production line startup, or multi-site manufacturing operations
* Proficiency with MRP/ERP, PLM, and Manufacturing Execution Systems

 

Base Pay Range for:

WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

**About Blue Origin** 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

 

As a Sr. Director for Manufacturing at Blue Origin’s manufacturing, production, and launch facilities, this role will have a direct impact on the success of Blue’s mission.

We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required.

 

**About This Opportunity** 
Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking an experienced Sr. Director with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of our rocket production program. This role will span the following functional areas:

Manufacturing and Integration
 
Provides senior leadership across production operations including structural fabrication, thermal protection systems, systems integration, testing, and final assembly for Blue Origin’s booster manufacturing. Responsible for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle. This role will also provide leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.

**Key Responsibilities:** 
Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:
 

* Lead and develop teams of Managers, Senior Managers, and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

 
**Minimum Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments

 

**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, the Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma; Black Belt certification preferred
* Experience transitioning manufacturing capabilities from development and prototyping into full-rate production
* Knowledge of fabrication processes including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and non-destructive testing
* Experience with facility activation, new production line startup, or multi-site manufacturing operations
* Proficiency with MRP/ERP, PLM, and Manufacturing Execution Systems

 

Base Pay Range for:

WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available 
 
CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No 
 
CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret 
 
TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description 
 
At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. 
 
 
 The Director, Manufacturing Engineering provides functional and strategic leadership for the manufacturing engineering organization, accountable for process capability, producibility, and product quality across production programs. This role leads a team of managers and engineers responsible for developing, deploying, and continuously improving manufacturing, test, and related industrial engineering processes to meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people objectives in Baltimore, MD .

 Key Responsibilities
 Functional & People Leadership Lead and develop a high‑performing manufacturing engineering organization, including managers, engineers, and supporting staff.
 Define and maintain functional standards, methods, tools, and best practices for manufacturing engineering across the site or business.
 Recruit, develop, and retain talent; drive succession planning, leadership development, and engagement/inclusion activities.
 Provide regular coaching, performance feedback, and career development for managers and engineers.
 
 
 Manufacturing Engineering Ownership Own manufacturing engineering processes from new product introduction through sustainment, ensuring robust process controls, standard work, and documented work instructions.
 Direct the creation and maintenance of MBOMs, routings, work instructions, tooling, and strategies that enable safe, efficient, and high‑quality production.
 Drive producibility into designs by partnering with Design Engineering early in the lifecycle; ensure effective transition to production and rate readiness.
 Establish and manage key performance indicators (yields, scrap, rework, cycle time, labor efficiency) and drive continuous improvement using data‑driven methods.
 
 
 Operations, Quality, and Continuous Improvement Partner closely with Operations, Quality & Mission Excellence, and Supply Chain to ensure stable processes and timely resolution of production issues.
 Oversee manufacturing engineering participation in MRB and nonconformance disposition; ensure effective root‑cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions.
 Champion initiatives to improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
 Lead manufacturing engineering support to factory readiness, capacity planning, and rate ramp‑ups.
 
 
 Program, Financial, and Strategic Management Align functional objectives, resources, and priorities with program and business needs; balance near‑term execution with long‑term capability development.
 Partner with Program Management and Business Management to support bids, proposals, and program execution, including manufacturing scope, risk, and cost/schedule inputs.
 Own manufacturing engineering budgets (labor, capital, and expense) and apply sound financial management.
 Develop and execute technology roadmaps and capital investment plans for manufacturing processes, equipment, and facilities.
 
 
 Compliance, Governance, and Stakeholder Management Ensure manufacturing engineering processes comply with regulatory requirements, customer standards, and internal procedures.
 Represent manufacturing engineering in internal and external reviews, audits, and customer engagements.
 Build strong relationships with sector/site leadership, program teams, and functional peers to drive alignment and resolve cross‑functional constraints.
 
 
 Basic Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 10 or more years of relevant experience; OR a Master’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 8 or more years of relevant experience.
 3 or more years of functional management experience leading organizations of at least 100 employees.
 Progressive leadership experience in manufacturing/production, operations, program management, testing, or a related area, including direct leadership of engineers and/or first‑line managers.
 Demonstrated experience in manufacturing or production engineering supporting complex hardware (e.g., aerospace, defense, electronics, or similar).
 Proven track record of improving manufacturing and test processes, yields, cycle times, and product quality using data and metrics.
 Working knowledge of manufacturing process controls, quality systems, and relevant industry/regulatory standards.
 Demonstrated financial acumen including budgets, rates, and cost management
 Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly present technical and operational content to leadership and customers.
 U.S. citizenship and an ability to obtain U.S. Government Secret security clearance or greater; OR DoE equivalent or greater
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Advanced degree in Engineering, Engineering Management, Business Administration, or related field.
 Experience in a Director or senior manager role leading a manufacturing engineering or test engineering organization in an aerospace/defense or similarly regulated environment.
 Experience working across multiple disciplines (design, manufacturing, and test engineering) with a strong focus on product development, producibility, and transition to production.
 Hands‑on experience with continuous improvement frameworks
 Experience managing capital equipment roadmaps and facilities upgrades to support long‑term manufacturing capacity and capability.
 Proven ability to build and develop high‑performing teams, including succession planning, leadership development, and engagement initiatives.
 Experience supporting proposals and customer reviews, including articulation of manufacturing engineering approaches, risks, and mitigations.
 Experience working in a matrixed organization, balancing program demands with functional standards and development needs.
 
 
 
Primary Level Salary Range: $194,600.00 - $292,000.00 
 
The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. 
 
Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. 
 
The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. 
 
Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**

Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

L3Harris is dedicated to recruiting and developing high-performing talent who are passionate about what they do. Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. Fundamental to our culture is an unwavering focus on values, dedication to our communities, and commitment to excellence in everything we do.
 
 
L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.
 
 
***Job Title: Director, Manufacturing Engineering***
***Job Code: 47622***
***Job Location: Camden, AR***
***Job Schedule: 4/10: Employees work 10 hour days, 4 days a week***
**Job Description:**
The Manufacturing Engineering Director in Camden, Arkansas will plan, organize and technically direct the manufacturing engineering activities and staff. Enable Operations to execute all programs in a safe and efficient manner, and ensuring the achievement of quality, cost and delivery schedule objectives. This position reports to the Senior Director Operations and Site Management. Our Camden, AR site is at $600M+ revenue and produces a diverse portfolio of highly engineered products for aerospace and defense applications. The individual will be responsible for implementing a disciplined operating system in line with the enterprise while improving the operating effectiveness of the site and leading an organization of over 190 people.
 
 
**Essential Functions:**

* 50% - Direct and lead technical team: Analyze, evaluate and determine appropriate solutions for manufacturing technical problems encountered in the application of manufacturing methods, facilities and processes. Apply engineering procedures, provide technical direction, create and apply work instructions and tooling for the factory floor. Participate in program and site corrective action boards and be a key member in customer escape and non-conformance investigations; develop direct cause, root cause and mistake proof corrective actions, as well as separation criteria when required. Ensure proper deployment of resources to achieve cost effective results in support of site and business unit deliverables. Direct the installation of Electronic Work Instructions (Platform is DELMIA) across the site and all product lines. Strict oversight of the Job Safety Analysis and Process Safety Management programs at the site.
* 15% - Administrative management: Ensure a safe work environment and remain in compliance to federal and local regulations. Develop long range technical and administrative plans, goals and strategies.
* 15% - Customer interface: Establish priorities to meet the needs of the customer and the organization with a dedication to support the manufacturing shop floor. Represent the organization as a prime internal and customer contact on manufacturing technical operations.
* 20% - Strategy and Continuous Improvement: Lead the sites Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) program. Drive operational

excellence throughout the organization and create a metrics driven, highly accountable mindset within the organization.
 
 

* Ability to obtain a US secret security clearance.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of 15 years prior relevant experience. Graduate Degree with a minimum of 13 years prior relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 19 years of prior relevant experience.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Demonstrated supervisory and leadership skills, including planning, organizing and directing activities; developing talent; and collaborating across business units and functional teams to achieve site objectives.
* Strong understanding of business development, program management, engineering, finance, operations

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**What To Expect**
Tesla is seeking a highly motivated Sr. Staff Manufacturing Engineer to build and lead a team of engineers focused on high-volume production launches. This role will drive the development of scalable manufacturing systems while collaborating with cross-functional teams to optimize product designs for manufacturability, accelerate assembly processes, and implement automation solutions. In this fast-paced, demanding environment, you’ll play a pivotal role in scaling Tesla’s SI robotics initiatives while advancing our mission to achieve sustainable abundance through innovative manufacturing practices.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Lead Manufacturing Engineering Team: Build, mentor, and scale high-performing teams to design and deploy high-volume production systems, ensuring alignment with Tesla’s speed and quality objectives
- Collaborate with Equipment Suppliers: Partner with internal and external suppliers to engineer, install, and validate production equipment, accelerating line ramp-up to meet volume targets
- Validate Requirements and Constraints: Use first principles analysis to rigorously assess product and process requirements, eliminating ambiguity and ensuring all elements are purpose-driven and essential
- Optimize Production Processes: Identify and remove non-value-added steps in workflows, prioritizing functional simplicity before pursuing automation or advanced optimization
- Improve Cycle Time: Analyze production bottlenecks and implement solutions to increase process speed, throughput, and overall line efficiency
- Deploy Automation Solutions: Strategically integrate automation as a final step after process simplification, ensuring systems are robust, high-speed, and scalable
- Ensure Seamless Operational Transitions: Coordinate with operations teams during ramp-up phases, delivering detailed documentation and training to sustain engineering teams for long-term success
**What You'll Bring**- First Principles Thinking: A rigorous mindset focused on breaking down complex problems to their fundamental truths, enabling innovative solutions to manufacturing challenges
- Proficiency in CAD tools (Catia and AutoCAD preferred) for designing and optimizing production systems
- Deep knowledge of mechanical assembly techniques (pressing, fastening, harnessing, etc.) and electrical integration, including quality control matrices, testing protocols, and troubleshooting methodologies
- Familiarity with torque tools, automation equipment, control systems, and communication protocols (e.g., PLC, HMI, SCADA)
- Production Transition Experience: Demonstrated success in scaling products from prototype to high-volume production, ensuring seamless handover to sustaining teams
- Resilience & Adaptability: Ability to thrive in high-pressure environments while managing competing priorities and tight deadlines
- Communication & Organization: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, paired with meticulous attention to detail and a highly organized approach to documentation and process handover
- Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical or Electrical engineering, or equivalent experience

- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction

- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**About us:**
At Plexus, our vision is to help create the products that build a better world. Driven by a passion for excellence, we partner with leading Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences and Industrial companies to design, manufacture and service some of the world’s most transformative products, including advanced surgical systems, diagnostic instruments, healthcare imaging equipment, mission critical aerospace systems, and electric vehicle (EV) charging solutions. Visit Plexus.com to learn more about our unwavering commitment to our vision.
 
 
**When we invest in our people, we invest in building a better world.**
With a vision rooted in the wellbeing and inclusive engagement of our team members, our customers, their end users and our communities, people are the heart of what we do and who we are. It is our values that unite us and guide us in everything that we do, including how we operate, behave and interact to foster a workplace where every team member feels valued and empowered to contribute their best.
 
 
Our values include: Growing our People, Building Belonging, Innovating Responsibly, Delivering Excellence and Creating Customer Success.
 
 
As a team member, you will engage in impactful work through global collaboration and the use of emerging technologies, join an inclusive culture where every team member is valued and working toward a greater purpose, and be empowered to reach your full potential through various development programs designed to accelerate your growth.
 
 
Plexus offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support team members' wellbeing, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, retirement savings, and opportunities for professional development. We also prioritize work-life balance and offer a variety of perks to enhance the team member experience. For more information, visit our US benefits website at usbenefits.plexus.com. Our commitment to pay range transparency fosters an equitable workplace, where everyone can feel valued. The annual compensation range for this position is stated below. The salary offered within this range will be based upon the geographic location, work experience, education, licensure requirements and/or skill level. Salary Range:
 
 
$132,500.00 - $198,700.00
 
 
**Purpose Statement:**
To provide leadership and direction to the Manufacturing Engineering team(s) from a functional perspective. Manage the Manufacturing Engineering function in line with functional specific strategies, process and systems development, people development, employee relations, plant level metrics.
 
 
**Key Job Accountabilities**

* Lead manufacturing-engineering excellence by collaborating with various functional leads to ensure engineering capability meets or exceeds manufacturing standards for quality product delivery.
* Support Program Management initiatives and activities to meet or exceed customer expectations.
* Lead process/product/equipment engineering activities in compliance with Plexus Core Values to meet industry standards, regulatory and customer requirements.
* Provide technical leadership to site operations, establish a technology roadmap, and collaborate with corporate and regional technical teams to achieve lower costs and higher manufacturing returns.
* Responsible to exemplify and hold their team accountable to demonstrating the Plexus Core Values. Leader will focus on evaluating potential, driving succession planning, and ensuring their employees receive the development and coaching required to realize their full potential.

**Education/Experience Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree with 8 or more years of related experience is preferred. An equivalent combination of education and/or experience will be considered.
* Proven leadership skills and management experience.

*This document does not represent a contract of employment and is not intended to capture every possible assignment the incumbent could be asked to perform.*

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**VP of Production**
--------------------

**Location:** Los Angeles, Detroit, or San Francisco 
**Employment:** Full time, in person 
**Base salary:** $200,000–$350,000 annually

American factories deserve a supply chain that moves as fast as they do. Nox Metals is building it, along with the tools that run it. We’re a technology company supplying raw metal to frontier American manufacturers. We use software and automation to supply metal to factories faster than the industry thought possible.

### **The role**

We’re hiring a VP of Production to lead manufacturing performance across Nox Metals’ facilities. You will own how work moves through our factories: production planning, daily execution, capacity, staffing, quality, productivity, and on-time delivery.

This is a hands-on manufacturing leadership role with real time on the factory floor. You will develop production leaders, resolve constraints, and create repeatable ways of working that help teams deliver as demand grows. Success means safe, reliable production and clear accountability from the daily schedule through completed customer orders.

### **You will**

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
**Quality Director**

**Aerospace Manufacturing | Senior Leadership Team**

**About Columbia Manufacturing**

Columbia Manufacturing, a member of Collective Manufacturing Group, produces complex fabricated components and assemblies for leading aerospace and power generation engine programs. We are committed to delivering safe, reliable, and compliant products while fostering a culture built on integrity, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

As we continue to grow, we are seeking a Quality Director who will strengthen our quality culture, develop our people, and help ensure we remain a trusted partner to our customers.

**Position Summary**

The Quality Director is a member of the senior leadership team responsible for ensuring Columbia Manufacturing consistently delivers products that meet customer, regulatory, and internal quality requirements.

This role goes beyond compliance. We are seeking a leader who combines sound judgment, ethical decision-making, objective interpretation of requirements, and strong cross-functional leadership. The successful candidate will guide the organization through customer requirements, industry standards, and business challenges while ensuring quality and integrity remain at the center of every decision. We believe strong teams produce strong results, and cultural fit is as important as technical expertise.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative leader who earns trust, develops people, and works effectively with Production, Engineering, Supply Chain, and customers. We value practical experience as highly as formal education and welcome candidates who have built their careers through hands-on manufacturing and quality leadership roles.

**What You’ll Do**

**Lead the Quality Management System**

* Maintain and continuously improve the Quality Management System.
* Ensure compliance with customer, regulatory, and aerospace requirements.
* Promote quality ownership and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

**Guide Quality Decisions**

* Interpret customer specifications, drawings, contractual requirements, and industry standards.
* Provide guidance when requirements are unclear, conflicting, or open to interpretation.
* Lead investigations, corrective actions, and nonconformance resolution using sound judgment and risk-based decision making.

**Partner with Customers and Regulatory Bodies**

* Serve as the primary quality representative to customers, auditors, and regulatory agencies.
* Build trusted relationships and lead internal, customer, and third-party audits.

**Develop People and Culture**

* Lead, mentor, and develop the Quality team.
* Build a high-performing organization through coaching, accountability, and succession planning.
* Foster collaboration and an environment where employees are comfortable raising concerns.
* Promote a culture where doing the right thing is always more important than meeting a schedule.

**Contribute to Business Success**

* Partner with Operations and Leadership to improve performance, reduce risk, strengthen organizational alignment, and support growth.
* Balance customer expectations, business priorities, and compliance requirements without compromising quality standards.
* Exercise independent quality authority and be willing to stop production or shipment when requirements have not been met.

**What We’re Looking For**

We recognize that great leaders come from many backgrounds. Candidates may have developed through engineering, manufacturing, inspection, quality systems, operations, military service, trade programs, or traditional degree pathways. Equivalent combinations of education, military training, trade experience, and hands-on manufacturing or quality leadership experience will be fully considered.

We are less concerned with how you gained your experience and more interested in your ability to lead people, interpret requirements, make sound decisions, and uphold quality standards under pressure.

Successful candidates will typically possess:

* Experience leading quality functions within aerospace, manufacturing, or other highly regulated industries.
* Strong understanding of quality systems, customer requirements, and specification interpretation.
* Demonstrated ethical leadership, sound decision-making, and the ability to uphold standards under pressure.
* Proven success leading teams and collaborating across departments.
* Strong communication skills and experience working with customers, auditors, and senior leadership.
* Continuous improvement mindset and practical problem-solving ability.

**Preferred Experience**

* Familiarity with aerospace quality standards such as AS9100, AS9110, AS13100, NADCAP, or customer-specific requirements.
* Experience supporting OEM customers such as GE Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, or similar organizations.
* Quality certifications or advanced education are valued but not required.

**Why This Role Matters**

The Quality Director plays a critical role in protecting our customers, our employees, and our reputation. This leader helps ensure that every product we build meets requirements and that every decision we make reflects our commitment to integrity, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**If you are a leader who values ethics, teamwork, sound judgment, and building strong people and processes, we encourage you to apply.**

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
***Title:*** ***Director of Quality, Regulatory and Improvement***

**Job Summary:**
----------------

This senior leadership role leads the quality departments for all Deringer-Ney locations globally. The Director implements best practices and metrics to coordinate all teams under a unified Quality Management System and is responsible for ensuring that the company's products, services, and manufacturing processes comply with strict government laws, industry standards, and internal quality systems. The role plans, coordinates, and directs the activities of the quality assurance and compliance programs to ensure the production of consistent, reliable products that meet or exceed established standards, and leads the continuous improvement team to support, train, and execute the DNIOS system.

***Supervisory Responsibilities:****Yes*

**Duties/Responsibilities:**
----------------------------

* Manage all quality departments by formulating, developing, and overseeing global goals, objectives, policies, procedures, systems, and outcomes pertaining to quality controls, assessments, and audits.
* Quality Management Systems (QMS): Build, maintain, and continuously improve QMS frameworks (such as ISO 13485 and ISO 9001).
* Develop a high-performance team by acquiring, developing, training, coaching, cultivating, and managing talented Quality Control personnel.
* Maintain and improve the quality system through routine system audits and corrective actions, and ensure that corrective actions, whether internal or external, are handled in a timely manner.
* Risk & Lifecycle Management: Oversee design controls, validation packages, complaint handling, and post-market surveillance (such as Automotive Reporting).
* Manage and maintain quality inspection and product release programs for raw materials, work in process (WIP), and finished goods.
* Regulatory Compliance & Filings: Lead product submissions and act as the primary liaison during agency audits.
* Disseminate quality awareness, adherence, and developments to global stakeholders by scheduling and performing regional quality audits and by ensuring that ISO systems are managed and maintained.
* Serve as an active member of the DNI Leadership Team, sharing the function's progress toward its goals while setting, and driving toward, an aspirational vision for a best-in-class quality department.
* Create a Cost of Poor Quality metric for the organization and set specific goals to improve quality performance across the company.
* Lead the development of the Annual Strategic Planning (P.D.C.A.) Cycle to include the Improvement Process.
* Lead the organization in attaining key metrics based on Balanced Scorecard (BSC) Objectives. Understand the department's key performance indicators and leading and lagging indicators, and contribute to achieving these goals, both individually and as a team.
* With the CIP Team, perform systematic audits designed to confirm that process standards are being utilized and met (BSC One-Page Reports).
* Interact with and make recommendations and presentations to the Executive Leadership Group via standardized checks: weekly, monthly, quarterly, and year-end. Maintain the PDCA Cycle while focusing on BSC Objectives.

**Required Skills/Abilities:**
------------------------------

* Strong background in ISO 9000 system management, including training and auditing.
* Strong background in ISO 13485 system management and thorough knowledge of FDA requirements and other international standards that regulate the medical device industry.
* Knowledge of automated inspection equipment, including vision systems and coordinate measuring devices.
* Adept at delegating and managing multiple tasks with various levels of priority.
* Excellent communication skills; must be able to present ideas, results, and requirements effectively throughout the organization and to the customer on a timely basis.
* Expert skill set in applied statistics, reliability, design of experiments, MSA, GR&R, and project management.
* Fluency with various software packages commonly used in project management, database, SPC, word processing, and data acquisition.
* Analytical, problem-solving, project management, facilitation, and decision-making skills are essential.
* Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate, coach, resolve conflict, and promote teamwork.
* Ability to see and hear the facts from several viewpoints while promoting success through interactive problem solving and teamwork.

**Experience & Education Requirements:**
----------------------------------------

* Technical degree (BS, BSE, or BSME) with a minimum of 10 years' experience in quality engineering or quality management.
* Strong preference for relevant industry experience in a metals or electrical connectors company or similar.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Control, or Regulatory Affairs within a regulated field such as medical devices, automotive, or defense.
* Preferred certifications: Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or Certified Quality Engineer (CQE).
* Demonstrated project management skills in the areas of process control, SPC, automotive PPAP submission, and statistical analysis.
* Lean Green Belt or Black Belt certification, Six Sigma, and DMAIC process experience.
* Actively continuing training through courses and seminars.

***Physical Requirements:***

* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times.
* Must be able to access and navigate each department at the organization’s facilities.
* Travel to other locations as required.

**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**Job Summary**

The Quality/CI Director is responsible for overseeing the overall quality management system and lean management systems, including the continuous development, improvement & maturity, and supporting the forward vision & business objectives of the segment. This position will support with a dotted-line, 40+ plant locations, and will work under the general direction of the Regional VPs.

 

**Principle Duties and Responsibilities**

* Oversees the overall quality management systems of the business segments and their impact on our business & customers.
* Oversees the overall continuous improvement program for the business segment through standardized practices, training, meeting improvement objectives, and continuing to mature our systems and capabilities.
* Assist the plant locations in maintaining compliance with the quality management system to ISO9001 requirements and sustaining our certification status.
* Assist quality & CI training to plant quality managers/coordinators as turnover occurs.
* Drive standardization into our quality management & lean management systems, ensuring best & consistent practices.
* Assist with new methodologies & technologies which impact quality & improvements (such as software & SCADA systems).
* Support onboarding of new and strategic customers within PPAP processes.
* Provide training & training material for the CI program & initiatives. Serve as coach & mentor for improvement projects.
* Host regional CI progress meetings with each region to help support progress & best practices.
* Take initiative on developing next steps & objectives to evolve & mature the effectiveness of our systems and provide necessary training.
Provide high level analysis from data/metrics of how effective our systems are and make recommendations and/or take action for improvement. 

 

**Qualifications**

* CQE ( *certified quality engineer* ) Certification Preferred or equivalent discipline body of knowledge.
* Minimum of five years of experience in Quality manufacturing environment is required.
* Working knowledge of ISO9001 QMS systems, and preferred understanding of IATF 16949 (formerly TS) & AIAG practices.
* Working knowledge of Quality Science applications.
* High-level understanding of lean concepts & applications.
* Six Sigma Black Belt preferred
* Working knowledge of Microsoft Office including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Access. NOTE! Must be proficient with charts & statistical formulas/templates in Excel.
Manager-level leadership knowledge/experience. 

*The Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer.*

Description:

**The Company:**

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.
* Develop Vendor Management metrics, analyze vendor performance and compliance trends, and lead a periodic cross-functional vendor review that feeds into Quality Management Review.
* Ensure inspection readiness in the vendor management function and assist function
