record.ROLE_TEXT:
At Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company (EBAD), we believe that our strengths are built on our most important resource - our people. Join EBAD and you'll be a part of a team who creates cutting edge technology that will blast us into the future. No other company can match the innovative energetic solutions that we provide. At EBAD you will actively contribute to successful missions putting men, women and satellites into space, and protecting our armed service men and women around the world. If this is the culture and work environment you are seeking, then EBAD is the place for you!
 
 
**Job Description**
**Location:**
Simsbury, CT
 
 
**Reports to:**
VP of Operations
 
 
**Industry:**
Aerospace & Defense
 
 
**Experience Level:**
Director (15+ years)
 
 
**Shape the Future. Deliver Excellence. Achieve Zero Failure.**
At
**Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense (EBAD),**
we’ve been innovating for nearly
**200 years,**
delivering mission-critical technologies that protect lives and advance exploration. As we prepare to double in size over the next 3–5 years, we’re investing in our people and culture to support this transformation.
 
 
We’re seeking a dynamic
**Director of Quality**
to lead a complex, multi-site quality organization and drive performance at scale. Based at our headquarters in Simsbury, Connecticut, this role is critical to ensure the highest levels of product integrity, compliance, and customer trust across a rapidly growing business. This is not just about maintaining standards but about building a future-state vision for quality that enables growth, safeguards mission success, and strengthens EBAD’s reputation as a trusted partner.
 
 
**The Opportunity:**
EBAD’s customers depend on us to deliver our products with zero failure in mission-critical environments. The Director of Quality will be responsible for developing and executing a strategic Quality Management System (QMS) while leading quality operations across multiple sites. This leader will be tasked with driving measurable quality improvement, while also championing a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
 
 
This is an exciting opportunity for a leader to make an immediate impact by providing direction, driving the strategy for the business, and developing a problem-solving culture.
 
 
**Core Competencies for Success:**

* Quality & Compliance Leadership: Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries, with expertise in zero-failure mission environments.
* Continuous Improvement & Performance: Skilled in EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices with the ability to drive metrics-based improvement and systemic problem-solving.
* Team Development & Leadership: Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and build strong teams while fostering engagement and accountability.
* Collaboration & Influence: Strong cross-functional partnership with credibility to influence senior leadership, customers, and suppliers.
* Resilience & Adaptability: Able to manage ambiguity, drive change, and motivate teams in a fast-scaling environment.

**The Candidate We Are Looking For:**

* BS in an engineering discipline (MS preferred)
* Minimum 10 years of experience in high-mix, low-volume operations and manufacturing environment
* Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other mission-critical industries
* Demonstrated expertise in leading audits and managing compliance across regulatory bodies, customers, and suppliers, with deep knowledge of standards such as AS9100, ISO9001, and DoD requirements
* Proven ability to enhance customer quality by partnering closely with engineering, operations, and supply chain teams to consistently meet customer demand
* Strong record of measurable quality improvements
* Skilled in continuous improvement, performance metrics, and problem-solving through EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practic

Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We're working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

 This role is part of Blue Origin's Launch Operations organization, where our focus is launching and recovering New Glenn safely, reliably, and at an ever-increasing cadence. Launch Operations owns everything required to turn a rocket into a flight-ready vehicle on the pad and to recover and refly it, from vehicle preparation and integration to pad operations and booster recovery.

 The 9x4 is the next step for New Glenn: a larger, more capable vehicle with a nine-engine booster, built, stacked, and launched vertically. The design decisions made about it now will determine, for the life of the program, how fast, how safely, and how reliably we can assemble, stack, and launch it. As Director of NG9x4 Vehicle Operations, you will be the single leader thinking about the 9x4 from the point of view of the people who will operate it, and the voice of Launch Operations in every decision meeting about the vehicle.
 Reporting to the Vice President of Launch Operations, you will start with a team of about a dozen engineers. Together you will evaluate the vehicle design and the concept of operations and shape both, help define and install the tooling and facilities in our new vertical integration facility, and write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for everything it takes to get the rocket to launch. Some of your scope will also reach the new launch pad being built for this vehicle. If you are successful, you will go on to build the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4.

 This is a mission-critical leadership role for Blue Origin. We need a leader who drives relentlessly toward results, unencumbered by the old way of doing things, and constantly inventing new ways to solve problems and perform our mission. This leader must not be afraid to get hands-on with engineers and technicians, on the tooling, in the facility, and eventually on the vehicle itself, when the mission requires it, including in the middle of the night. At the same time, your long-term measure of success is building in, from the start, a vehicle and a set of processes that let the Launch Operations teams assemble, stack, and launch at a fast, repeatable, "boring" cadence. You'll make the impossible look routine through detailed, quantitative, hands-on command of the work your team executes down to the individual work order.
 


 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 Be the Voice of Operations on the 9x4 
 Represent Launch Operations in all design, configuration, and readiness decisions for the vehicle, bringing the perspective of the people who will assemble, stack, and launch it
 Evaluate the vehicle design and challenge requirements, driving design changes that make final assembly of the booster, stacking, and launch easier, faster, and safer
 Bring the lessons learned from today's horizontal integration operations into the design of vertical operations, and question which of them still apply
 Partner with vehicle design and engineering, facility, and pad teams so that operations needs are in the design before changes become expensive
 Stand Up Vertical Operations 
 Help shape the tooling, ground support equipment, and other installations in the new vertical integration facility, and help get them procured and installed
 Formalize the concept of operations in greater detail: how the nine-engine booster is finally assembled, how the second stage and payload are stacked vertically, and how the vehicle is prepared and launched
 Write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for all of the preparation needed to get the rocket to launch, and set the standard for high-quality, executable work orders (clear, sequenced, measurable, and completable by shift) so launch readiness is derived from objective data
 Take on operations scope for work at the new launch pad being built for this vehicle
 Lead Execution and Manage Risk 
 Manage technical and schedule risk as the vehicle, the facility, and the tooling come together; when schedule slips, personally own and drive the recovery plan rather than simply reporting the slip
 Perpetuate a high-standard safety culture across all vehicle work, given the significant personnel, process, and material hazards involved
 Be willing to get on the ground with engineers and technicians to solve problems directly, at any hour, when the mission requires it
 Drive Cross-Functional Integration 
 Serve as the primary point of contact between the operations teams and New Glenn vehicle design/engineering, facility, tooling, and pad leadership
 Partner with the business operations function (scheduling and operations analytics) to maintain an objective, data-driven view of remaining work and schedule risk
 Build the organization's own engineering ownership and judgment over time, reducing reliance on borrowed engineering support from other Blue Origin programs
 Build and Lead a High-Performing Organization 
 Lead an initial team of about a dozen engineers, and grow it into the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4
 Build, mentor, and develop a bench of leaders and engineers in a fast-growing organization
 Take difficult, immature processes and mature them into fast, repeatable operations that don't require nightly heroics to execute
 Foster a culture where every technician and engineer is genuinely excited about Blue Origin's mission and understands the "why" behind the work
 Champion the use of AI to reduce engineering workload (including work-order authoring) and to accelerate the ramp of less experienced engineers
 Deliver Results 
 Use your own data and numerical analysis to understand team performance, drive decisions, and communicate progress
 Set quantitative targets for the labor hours and calendar time to assemble, stack, and launch the 9x4, and shape the vehicle and the processes to meet them, so the vehicle supports a much higher launch cadence
 Present vehicle design, readiness, and risk to Blue Origin's most senior executive leadership, including with little to no coaching
 
 WHAT YOU BRING

 Minimum Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience building and leading complex vehicle or aircraft programs
 7+ years of progressive leadership experience building, integrating, or maintaining complex vehicles, aircraft, or other high-reliability systems: aerospace, defense, marine, oil & gas, or similar heavy/complex-machine environments
 Experience representing operations, manufacturing, or production in design decisions, with a demonstrated track record of challenging engineering requirements and driving design changes to improve manufacturability or maintainability
 Leadership experience with budget and resource management responsibility for technical/operational organizations
 Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams, with the ability to grow a team and lead through subordinate managers
 A specific, demonstrated track record of driving measurable rate or throughput improvements in a complex manufacturing, assembly, or operations environment
 A demonstrated track record of building and perpetuating a high-standard safety culture in environments with significant personnel, process, or material hazards
 Demonstrated ability to make high-stakes technical and operational decisions under schedule pressure
 Strong executive presence with excellent written and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels, including senior executive leadership
 Strategic thinker with a bias for action and a track record of hands-on operational execution
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Direct experience in final assembly, integration, or maintenance of military or civilian aircraft, weapons systems, or launch vehicles
 Experience with vertical assembly or stacking of large vehicles or structures, such as launch vehicles, or comparable heavy lifting and integration
 Experience standing up a new factory, production line, or facility, including shaping the tooling and the concept of operations
 Experience writing the first work instructions or work orders for a new vehicle or product
 A track record of taking a new vehicle, aircraft, or complex product from first-unit production to rate production
 Hands-on experience as an aircraft mechanic (or similar trade) and/or as a manufacturing engineer
 Working knowledge of aerospace standards and workmanship requirements
 Experience building or scaling an engineering/technical organization from a nascent, dependent state to self-sufficiency
 Master's degree in a related engineering field, or an MBA
 Culture Statement 
 Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Export Control Regulations 
 Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 Background Check 
 Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
 Required for Certain Job Profiles:  Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
 Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
 Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
 
 Benefits 
 Benefits include:  Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
 Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
 Paid Time Off:  Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
 Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here .

 Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation 
 Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at  EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Shield AI is seeking a Strategy & Operations Director to help define enterprise strategy and ensure its operational execution. This role offers immersive exposure to the company’s most critical decisions — spanning aircraft systems, AI software (Hivemind), autonomy hardware, and international growth.

As a core member of the Strategy & Operations team, you’ll apply structured problem‑solving, financial rigor, and operational discipline to turn strategic priorities into actionable, measurable outcomes. The role combines high‑performance expectations with a strong learning and development environment — ideal for professionals seeking to grow into future strategy, operations, or general management leaders.

What you'll do:

 - Enterprise Strategy Development:
 
 - Lead the multi‑year strategic planning and annual operating strategy cycles.
 
 - Evaluate portfolio tradeoffs across platforms, software, hardware, and emerging growth vectors.
 
 - Conduct market sizing, competitive analysis, and scenario modeling across U.S. and allied defense markets.
 
 Capital Allocation & Business Case Rigor:
 
 - Build financial models and analytic frameworks for investment decisions (new platforms, manufacturing, international expansion).
 
 - Assess TAM, margin structure, capital intensity, payback, and risk‑adjusted returns.
 
 - Contribute to the development of enterprise‑wide capital allocation frameworks and governance processes.
 
 Operationalization of Strategy:
 
 - Translate strategic priorities into cross‑functional execution plans with defined KPIs and milestones.
 
 - Track and report on progress through structured operating cadences (monthly and quarterly performance reviews).
 
 - Identify bottlenecks, analyze root causes, and recommend actionable solutions to sustain execution velocity.

Required qualifications:

 - Min 12+ years of experience with Bachelors, 8+ with Masters, and 5+ with PhD.

 - Min 4+ years’ experience in a top-tier strategy consulting, corporate strategy or other high‑rigor roles.

 - Strong analytical and conceptual problem‑solving abilities.

 - Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive insight through analysis.

 - Financial modeling and analytical capability (unit economics, forecasting, scenario analysis).

 - Experience or strong interest in complex, technical, or regulated industries (aerospace, defense, AI, or advanced manufacturing preferred).

 - Ability to work collaboratively across teams and influence senior stakeholders.

 - U.S. citizenship required (ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance).

The Plant Manager is the senior leader on site and is responsible for everything that goes on inside the fence-line and is the driver of the production process. We look to the Plant Manager to build a collaborative environment between operations, sales, engineering, accounting, and transportation. This dynamic leader will be pushing continuous improvement in workplace safety, production efficiency, product cost, and customer service.

**Job Location**

This position will be located at our plant in Sweetwater, TN.

**Job Responsibilities**

 

* Ensure the plant employees and guests on site comply with safety and environmental practices – lead by example and build a safety first culture.
* Lead production scheduling to meet customer needs including timely delivery.
* Develop a keen focus on customer service and proactive communication across the team.
* Partner with the engineering team to ensure proper drawings and designs are being used during the manufacturing process.
* Purchase material/services to successfully operate the facility.

* Be a leader and coach leadership. Motivate crews during morning huddles. Lead effective Mid-Day meetings. Coach Leads on how to set expectations on a whiteboard and have them followed. Lead inventory counts. Promote safety best practices in meetings with other Plant Managers.
* Perform any other duties as assigned by the General Manager as deemed appropriate and necessary by them.

**Job Requirements**

 

* Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Engineering or equivalent experience
* 10+ years of experience working in a leadership role in an industrial manufacturing environment
* Experience with precast/concrete or building materials is a plus
* Proven track record of developing, leading and maintaining a continuous improvement mindset at the plant

* Ability to work with computer as necessary (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, AX)
* Ability to lead and direct other individuals and work with other group leaders

* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.  

 The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities:  we come together ,  we always look for a better way , and  we create possibilities . 

 Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

 Interested in joining us on our journey? 

The Manufacturing Quality Director provides strategic leadership and oversight of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational excellence, product reliability, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement. This position is responsible for developing and executing quality strategies, driving improvements in internal and external quality metrics, and reducing the overall cost of quality.
As a key member of the plant leadership team, the Manufacturing Quality Director partners with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Product Management, Supplier Quality, Technology, Distribution, and Service to establish quality objectives, resolve complex quality issues, and ensure alignment with business priorities.
The Director is accountable for manufacturing quality performance, execution of the quality operating plan, continuous improvement initiatives, and leadership and development of the Quality organization.
This role supports plant operations in LaFayette, GA. 
 Position 
Manufacturing Quality Director 
 Location 
USA, LaFayette, GA 
 
 How You'll Create Possibilities 
 Quality Strategy and Operational Leadership 
 Develop and execute manufacturing quality strategies aligned with plant and business objectives.
 Provide leadership and direction for quality performance across manufacturing operations.
  
 Establish measurable quality objectives, performance targets, and improvement plans to support operational excellence.
 Partner with plant leadership and cross-functional teams to integrate quality requirements into manufacturing processes and business decisions.
 Drive accountability for quality performance through effective communication, performance reviews, and corrective action plans.
 Promote a culture of quality ownership, continuous improvement, and proactive problem-solving throughout the organization.
  
 Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement 
  
 Own and drive improvement of key internal and external quality metrics, including First Pass Yield (FPY), Cost of Quality (COQ), Service Call Rate (SCR), scrap, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), and product damage.
 Analyze quality performance data to identify trends, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.
 Lead the development and execution of corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans to address quality concerns and prevent recurrence.
 Ensure timely containment, root cause analysis, and permanent corrective actions for End-of-Line Audit (EOLA) findings and other manufacturing quality issues.
 Drive year-over-year improvements in quality performance, process capability, and manufacturing efficiency.
 Champion Lean principles, structured problem-solving, error-proofing (poka-yoke), and proactive quality tools to reduce defects and improve process reliability.
  
 Cost of Quality and Financial Accountability 
 Own the development and execution of the manufacturing Cost of Quality operating plan.
 Identify and prioritize opportunities to reduce scrap, rework, warranty exposure, product damage, and other quality-related costs.
 Establish improvement initiatives targeting the highest contributors to quality losses.
 Partner with Operations, Finance, Engineering, and other stakeholders to evaluate financial impacts and deliver sustainable cost reductions.
 Monitor performance against quality cost targets and implement corrective actions to address unfavorable trends.
 Drive resolution of quality-related concessions attributable to manufacturing operations and implement strategies to prevent recurrence.
  
 Quality Management Systems and Process Control 
 Ensure manufacturing operations comply with established Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, applicable ISO standards, and internal quality procedures.
 Provide oversight of the Manufacturing Change Process (MCP), ensuring changes are appropriately evaluated, documented, approved, communicated, and implemented.
 Partner with the Change Implementation Board (CIB) and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain effective change control and documentation compliance.
 Identify critical manufacturing processes requiring control plans and ensure appropriate controls are established, documented, and maintained.
 Ensure manufacturing quality standards, procedures, and control plans remain current and are consistently followed.
 Support continuous improvement of quality systems, process controls, and manufacturing standards to minimize operational risk.
  
 Cross-Functional Quality and Customer Support 
  
 Collaborate with Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Product Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Field Quality, Distribution, and Service to resolve quality issues impacting manufacturing operations and customers.
 Partner with Supplier Quality to address supplier-related defects, assess proposed supplier changes, and ensure appropriate change control and production readiness.
 Work with Field Quality and Service organizations to identify emerging product concerns, evaluate field performance, and implement effective manufacturing countermeasures.
 Ensure appropriate quality controls are established for product rework, reprogramming, and corrective actions performed at supplier facilities, distribution centers, or other locations.
 Support resolution of Technical Assistance Group (TAG) concerns and other field service issues attributable to manufacturing processes.
 Collaborate with Engineering to recommend improvements to product testing requirements and manufacturing controls based on field performance and customer usage.
 Leverage technical expertise across the organization to accelerate problem resolution and achieve quality objectives.
  
 People Leadership and Organizational Development 
 Lead, develop, and manage the Manufacturing Quality organization, including Quality Leaders, Quality Engineers, technical specialists, and other supporting personnel.
 Establish clear performance expectations, responsibilities, and development objectives aligned with departmental and business priorities.
 Provide coaching, mentoring, and performance feedback to strengthen technical capabilities, leadership effectiveness, and accountability.
 Ensure appropriate staffing, resource allocation, and prioritization of quality initiatives to meet operational requirements.
 Build a high-performing quality organization focused on collaboration, continuous improvement, and measurable results.
 Promote employee engagement, knowledge sharing, and the development of future quality leaders.
  
 Performance Monitoring and Business Reporting 
 Establish and maintain effective daily, weekly, and monthly quality performance reviews.
 Monitor key performance indicators, identify unfavorable trends, and ensure timely escalation and resolution of significant quality concerns.
 Communicate quality performance, improvement initiatives, risks, and corrective action progress to plant and business leadership.
 Translate complex quality data into actionable business insights and improvement priorities.
 Ensure quality initiatives are executed within established timelines, budgets, and performance expectations.
  
 Leadership Expectations 
  
 Demonstrate ownership and accountability for manufacturing quality performance.
 Influence decisions and drive results across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Balance immediate operational quality requirements with long-term strategic improvement objectives.
 Exercise sound judgment in evaluating quality risks, business impacts, and resource priorities.
 Foster collaboration, operational discipline, and continuous improvement.
 Develop organizational capability through effective leadership, talent development, and succession planning.
 
 
 What You'll Bring to Our Team 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline; equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience may be considered.
 Experience in Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Reliability, Product Service, or a related technical function.
 Demonstrated experience with root cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies.
 Ability to analyze technical and quality data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Demonstrated ability to work effectively across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and technical investigations simultaneously.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and PowerPoint.
 Knowledge of PFMEA, Control Plans, CAPA, SPC, and other quality systems and tools.
 Experience supporting New Product Introduction and product reliability initiatives.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

 DIRECTOR, POWER PLANT OPERATIONS 

 The Director, Memphis Power Plant Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the gas turbine power generation facility supporting SpaceXSI's Colossus data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee. This role oversees all plant operations, maintenance, commissioning, and continued construction/expansion of the dedicated power plant, with full ownership of delivering reliable, high-availability electrical power to the Colossus AI training clusters. The position is responsible for driving operational excellence, ensuring 24/7 power reliability and quality, safety, environmental compliance, and leading cross-functional teams to achieve aggressive scale-up, availability, cost, and schedule objectives in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Memphis gas turbine power plant, including 24/7 operations, maintenance, commissioning, and ongoing construction and capacity expansion

 Own end-to-end delivery of electrical power to the Colossus data center sites, ensuring industry-leading reliability, availability, power quality, and redundancy

 Lead multidisciplinary teams of operators, maintenance technicians, engineers, contractors, and support staff in a 24/7 operational and construction environment

 Oversee plant performance, commissioning, testing, and seamless integration with data center electrical infrastructure and load

 Develop and execute comprehensive operations and maintenance strategies, including preventative/predictive maintenance, outage planning, hot gas path management, and OEM coordination for gas turbines, generators, balance of plant, and high-voltage electrical systems

 Manage concurrent construction, equipment installation, civil works, and phased capacity expansions while maintaining safe, reliable operation of the existing plant

 Ensure full compliance with environmental, safety, and regulatory requirements, including air permits, emissions controls, TDEC, EPA, OSHA, and local authorities

 Partner closely with SpaceXSI data center operations, engineering, fuel suppliers, OEMs, utilities, and regulatory agencies

 Formulate and execute operating budgets, fuel management, O&M, capital projects, and annual operating plans

 Drive continuous improvement in plant availability, heat rate, emissions, cost, safety metrics, and operational processes

 Establish and promote a culture of uncompromising safety, accountability, operational excellence, rapid execution, and collaboration

 Serve as the site leader and primary representative to the Memphis community, regulators, and stakeholders

 Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing talent; manage staffing, resource allocation, and contractor oversight for both operations and construction

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, or other engineering discipline

 8+ years of experience in power generation operations, plant management, or industrial or aerospace operations

 5+ years of leadership experience managing teams of operators, technicians, and engineers

 Experience operating or managing gas turbine power plants (simple cycle or combined cycle)

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Experience managing large-scale gas turbine facilities (100 MW+), preferably with high-availability critical power applications (data centers, industrial, or similar)

 Proven track record of achieving and sustaining high plant availability, reliability, and low forced outage rates

 Hands-on experience with plant construction, commissioning, start-up, and concurrent operations/expansion of gas turbine facilities

 Deep knowledge of gas turbine technology (aeroderivative and/or heavy-duty frames), performance optimization, emissions controls (SCR, etc.), and balance of plant systems

 Experience with high-voltage electrical systems, generators, switchgear, protection, and data center or industrial interconnection

 Strong understanding of environmental permitting, air quality compliance, and regulatory reporting for combustion turbines

 Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments requiring simultaneous operations and major construction

 Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, fuel costs, contractors, and complex stakeholder relationships

 Excellent oral and written communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills

 Unfazed by major, abrupt changes in strategic direction or aggressive timelines

 Ability to work in a demanding, autonomously driven, start-up atmosphere

 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 Ability to support and supervise plant operations and construction outside of normal business hours, including nights, weekends, and on-call response

 Must be based at the Memphis, TN site

 Willingness to work extended hours as needed to support plant reliability and construction milestones

 General physical fitness required; ability to walk the plant site, access equipment, and work in industrial/outdoor environments (heat, noise, etc.)

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.
 
 Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.
 
 We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

 Job Description 
 

 Key Responsibilities: 
 GMP Operations Quality Oversight 
 ·        Provide Quality Assurance oversight of GMP Manufacturing and QC testing operations through the product lifecycle from master cell bank to drug product.
 ·        Provide Quality Assurance strategy and oversight of external QC laboratories, ensuring method lifecycle activities (qualification, verification, and validation) are executed in compliance with cGMP, ICH, and internal quality standards, with appropriate review and approval of protocols, reports, and methods.
 ·        Review and approve laboratory investigations (e.g., OOS/OOT/deviations) conducted by contract partners, ensuring thorough root cause analysis, robust corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and aligned decision-making impacting product quality and disposition.
 ·        Apply Quality Risk Management principles to oversee risk assessments in collaboration with Manufacturing, and QC operations.
 ·        Partner with cross-functional teams to identify, assess, and mitigate quality risks impacting product quality, patient safety, and supply continuity.
 ·        Ensure quality risk decisions are appropriately justified, documented, and aligned with internal procedures and regulatory expectations.
 ·        Partner with Manufacturing operations and QC to resolve quality issues arising during manufacturing, laboratory activities and material receipt and shipping. Oversee implementation and manufacturing workflow development for the startup of digital manufacturing and data solutions in collaboration with manufacturing, automation, engineering, and information technology teams.
 ·        Review and approve manufacturing and test records, deviations, investigations, change controls, and CAPA to ensure product quality and support timely product disposition.
 ·        Evaluate operational and quality risks related to new product introduction.
 Compliance, Audits & Inspections 
 ·        Participate in internal GMP audits and routine walk-throughs of Manufacturing, QC, and Warehouse areas to support continuous improvement.
 ·        Serve as a key Quality contact during regulatory inspections and internal audits, including preparation and response to findings.
 ·        Monitor regulatory requirements and proactively assess potential operational compliance risks.
 Quality Systems & Documentation 
 ·        Approve GMP documentation including risk assessments, procedures, master batch records, specifications, and analytical methods. Drive continuous improvement of quality processes supporting GMP operations.
 Leadership & Collaboration 
 ·        Provide leadership, development, and mentoring for Quality personnel supporting GMP operations.
 ·        Partner cross-functionally with Manufacturing, QC, Process Development, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality management on corporate and site initiatives.
 ·        Lead or support Quality-related operational projects and improvement initiatives.
 ·        Provide on-call Quality Assurance support to Manufacturing and QC operations, as required.
 ·        Use risk-based decision making to prioritize tasks and ensure product quality.
 ·        Maintain strong working knowledge of Health Canada, FDA, and global GMP expectations.

 Knowledge: 
 ·        Demonstrates in-depth knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) and/or Good Laboratory Practices (GLPs).
 ·        Demonstrates in-depth knowledge of QA principles, concepts, industry practices, and standards.
 ·        Demonstrates keen understanding of Computer Systems Validation and ICH Guidelines.
 ·        Demonstrates excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills.
 ·        Demonstrates knowledge of Six Sigma, Define-Measure-Analyze-Improve-Control (DMAIC) methodology, performance measures and quality improvement statistical.
 ·        Demonstrates working knowledge of Risk Management tools (e.g., Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) and / or Failure Mode Effects Analysis (FMEA)).
 ·        Certification by ASQ (Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Quality Engineer, and Certified Quality Manager) or other industry-recognized professional organizations.
 
 Specific Education & Experience Requirements: 
 ·        10+ years of relevant experience in a GMP environment related field and a Bachelor’s degree in science or related field OR 
 ·        8+ years of relevant experience and a MS OR 
 ·        5+ years of relevant experience and a PharmD/ PhD
 ·        Extensive hands-on experience supporting biologics, GMP Manufacturing and QC operations is required.
 ·        Proven experience leading investigations, CAPA, and change management in a GMP operational environment is required.
 ·        Strong understanding and experience of materials management, manufacturing and analytical methods and testing systems within a GMP environment.
 ·        Previous experience in people management within Quality is required.
 ·        Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills are required.

 Preferred: 
 ·        Experience supporting Health Canada, FDA, or other regulatory inspections
 People Leader Accountabilities:  
 ·        Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams. 
 ·        Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose. 
 ·        Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem. 
 
 
The salary range for this position is: $182,070.00 - $235,620.00. Gilead considers a variety of factors when determining base compensation, including experience, qualifications, and geographic location. These considerations mean actual compensation will vary. This position may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus, discretionary stock-based long-term incentives (eligibility may vary based on role), paid time off, and a benefits package. record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. Whether that means specialized training, a clearly laid out career trajectory or collaborating cross-functionally, we are committed to the success of our people the same way we’ve been committed to the success of the El Pollo Loco brand for the last 50 years. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
 
 
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
 
 
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
 
 
Let’s Get Loco!
 
 
What’s in it for you!
 
 

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:** 
The Senior Director, Quality Assurance owns El Pollo Loco's enterprise quality assurance function end to end, consolidating vendor-level quality assurance and regulatory food safety compliance into a single point of accountability. This role is responsible for the integrity of the supply chain's quality systems — from supplier and co-manufacturer qualification through regulatory compliance across federal, state, and local agencies — and serves as the primary quality and food safety resource to the franchise system.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 
Vendor & Supplier Quality Assurance
 

* Directs vendor and supplier quality assurance programs across El Pollo Loco's poultry portfolio, including fresh leg quarters (“Saddles”) and value-added further-processed chicken items, ensuring specification integrity, ingredient consistency, and product quality at every stage of the supply chain.
* Leads vendor qualification, audit, scorecarding, and corrective-action programs; partners with Procurement and Distribution to resolve quality holds, non-conformances, and supplier performance issues.
* Owns quality specifications for co-manufactured and further-processed chicken products, working directly with processors to validate manufacturing controls, shelf-life, and food safety design prior to system-wide rollout.
* Evaluates and approves new vendors, ingredients, and product formulations, ensuring alignment with brand quality standards and regulatory requirements.

Regulatory & Food Safety Compliance
 

* Serves as the company's senior point of accountability for food safety regulatory compliance, including FDA, USDA, FSMA, HACCP, GFSI, and state and local health department requirements across all operating jurisdictions.
* Builds and maintains direct working relationships with state and federal regulatory agencies; leads the company's response to regulatory inquiries, inspections, and enforcement actions.
* Owns crisis management, product withdrawal, and recall protocols (including activation of the Level 3 Withdrawal Process), partnering with executive leadership and legal counsel as needed.
* Directs internal and third-party food safety audit programs spanning restaurants, distribution centers, and manufacturing partners.

Team Leadership & Franchise Support
 

* Builds, leads, and develops a high-performing QA organization spanning both vendor quality and regulatory food safety disciplines; sets performance expectations, coaching plans, and succession pipelines for direct reports.
* Serves as a critical QA partner to the franchise system, delivering training, technical guidance, and responsive support to franchisees on quality and food safety matters.
* Represents Quality Assurance in cross-functional and executive leadership forums, translating vendor and regulatory risk into clear, actionable guidance for Operations and senior leadership.
* Other duties as assigned by the SVP, Supply Chain & Quality Assurance.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
 
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
 
 
**Education/Work Experience:** 
BA/BS in Food Science, Food Microbiology, or a related field required; Master's degree preferred. Minimum 12+ years of progressive quality assurance and food safety experience, with substantial, direct experience in poultry and value-added/further-processed chicken products required. Demonstrated background working directly with state and federal regulatory agencies (FDA, USDA, state health departments) on compliance, inspections, or enforcement matters required. Prior experience directly managing and developing a quality assurance team required.
 
 
**License/Certifications:** 
Valid driver's license required. HACCP certification required; PCQI (Preventive Controls Qualified Individual) preferred.
 
 
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:** 

* Proven track record building, managing, and developing high-performing quality assurance teams, with strong people-leadership, coaching, and succession-planning skills.
* Deep working knowledge of value-added and further-processed chicken manufacturing, including co-manufacturer oversight, specification management, and shelf-life validation.
* Established credibility with state and federal regulatory agencies; skilled at navigating inspections, audits, and enforcement proceedings with composure and precision.
* Demonstrated ability to support and train franchisees on quality and food safety standards, balancing brand protection with practical, field-level guidance.
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives; decisive and able to make fact-based decisions under pressure.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail.
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners, including vendors, regulators, and franchisees.
* Ability to prioritize and plan competing, time-sensitive work assignments under frequent, tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex regulatory reports, contracts, and correspondence.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significant risk and consequence to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state vendor, distribution, and restaurant locations, as needed, by car or airplane.

Our Company
 
 
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. Today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide our customers with Quality Chicken. Fast. Easy. Affordable.
 
 
PAY DISCLAIMER – CA ONLY
 
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. At El Pollo Loco, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range. Individual pay decisions will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
At Elanco (NYSE: ELAN) – it all starts with animals! 
 
 As a global leader in animal health, we are dedicated to innovation and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People. 
 
 At Elanco, we pride ourselves on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment. We believe that diversity is the driving force behind innovation, creativity, and overall business success. Here, you’ll be part of a company that values and champions new ways of thinking, work with dynamic individuals, and acquire new skills and experiences that will propel your career to new heights. 
 
 Making animals’ lives better makes life better – join our team today! 
 
 
 The Director, TSMS is responsible for all technical aspects of product and process performance at the Elwood, Kansas monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing facility.  The role is responsible for maintaining and improving the scientific oversight of the manufacturing processes and technical changes, and to ensure the product stewardship across process units and functions.

 In direct collaboration with Manufacturing Operation units and other functions (Quality, Engineering, IT, etc.) the Director, TSMS provides clear direction and the necessary expertise to:
 Ensure the robustness of manufacturing and packaging processes so that all products and processes are maintained in an appropriately validated state of control throughout the product lifecycle. Support and where appropriate lead optimization of biopharmaceutical processes by applying sound scientific reasoning (first principles) and following integrated process and technology strategies. Identify and continuously apply best practices specifically in training, process changes and handling of discrepancy and investigation resolution. Coach and develop TSMS Team members to identify strengths and weaknesses and grow the technical ability of the team.

 Functions, Duties, Tasks :
 Ensure that the technical competencies/knowledge for the site’s monoclonal antibody processes, raw materials, sterile processes, and primary packaging components are in place (as applicable).
 Advises, guides and coaches TSMS associates for the purpose of ensuring routine operational support, identifying solutions and improvement, solving problems, decision making and communication including quality of written reports.
 Ensures adherence to cGMP requirements, guidelines, SOPs, as well as compliance to local laws, the Elanco Red Book, company policies and Health Safety & Environment (HSE) requirements. Particular attention is given to the protection of employees, patients, company assets and the environment.
 Ensure that mAb products and processes are in control and capable, with appropriate control strategies in place to meet Elanco Global Quality and Manufacturing standards and maintain continuity of supply.
 Develop and lead continuous improvement initiatives which positively impact cycle time, productivity, process robustness, gross margin, and production capacity.
 Partner with Commercialization, R&D, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain and Quality to successfully in-transfer new mAb products.  Ensure that transfers are accomplished on-time, with appropriate process / product control strategies in place.
 Leads cross functional teams for root cause investigations.
 Committed to knowledge sharing/transfer inside site manufacturing groups as well as to Technical R&D (TRD).
 Drives the product control strategy including development and application of KPIs to enable meaningful CPP/CQA trending and reporting of key process data as well as to quickly identify changing quality trends and issues.
 Develop the expense and capital planning budgets for the TSMS function in collaboration with the Sr. Director, Commercialization and site leadership team.  Ensure TSMS delivery meets or exceeds financial commitments.
 Responsible for the design and delivery of TSMS owned technical training programs as well as appropriate technical on-boarding to ensure competency of TSMS associates.
 Stays abreast of technological, regulatory and industry developments, e.g., via internal and external benchmarking.
 Build and grow the TSMS function, recruiting and developing talent in alignment with the site’s strategic needs.
 Maintain a safe work environment and establish a strong safety culture in compliance with Elanco standards and all applicable government requirements.
 Ensure TSMS staff operate in accordance with all applicable Quality and cGMP requirements.  Accountable for quality performance of the function and delivery against site quality targets.
 Develop and review operational objectives with direct reports, establish appropriate talent development plans, and conduct staff performance management reviews as required.
 Other duties as required.
 
 Minimum Qualification (education, experience and/or training, required certifications) :
 Bachelor’s degree in a biomanufacturing related discipline (e.g. biology, Chemistry, engineering, etc.).
 10 years of related working experience
 5+ years’ experience in technical management position.
 5+ years’ experience in (bio)pharmaceutical formulation, process development, or manufacturing technology.
 Ability to lead and develop a team.
 Fundamental understanding of (bio)pharmaceutical analytical testing.
 Demonstrated understanding of Q culture, cGMP standards, and regulatory regulations.
 
 Additional Preferences :
 MSc in Science, Pharmacy, Mechanical or Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Technology.
 Proficiency in applied statistics/Lean Six Sigma methodologies.
 Understanding of USDA, FDA, and EU GMP regulatory standards for veterinary biologics.
 Demonstrated problem solving experience, identifying and understand issues, problems, and opportunities.
 Ability to network and build strong, collaborative relationships across functions / geographies.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills (English).
 Strong mentoring and coaching skills
 
 Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown underrecognized groups are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Elanco we are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive work environment. If you think you might be a good fit for a role but don't necessarily meet every single qualification, we encourage you to apply. You may be the right candidate for this role or other roles!

 Elanco Benefits and Perks: 
 We offer a comprehensive benefits package focusing on financial, physical, and mental well-being while encouraging our employees to pursue our purpose! Some highlights include:
 Multiple relocation packages
 8-week parental leave
 9 Employee Resource Groups
 Annual bonus offering
 Flexible work arrangements
 Up to 6% 401K matching
 
 #LI-Onsite
#LI-HL
 
 Elanco is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status 
 
 Elanco may use automated tools, including AI, to support parts of our recruitment process, such as reviewing applications against job‑related criteria and/or transferrable skills. These tools help ensure a consistent, structured evaluation, but they do not make hiring decisions. All decisions involve a human reviewer. For more information on how we handle personal data, please see our Elanco Workforce Privacy Notice.
